table_head:
| ID | Issue | Status | Plan | Sub-issues | Blocked | Detail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
notice: > Generated by `foreman backlog` from `{file}`: do not edit by hand (`foreman backlog --help`).
decisions_intro: Questions only {owner} can answer; each one names its options.
resume: You are the orchestrator of this session ({procedure}). Pick up without asking: read your board, check the live agents and background tasks, and carry on with «Next».
guard_lock: Blocked by the foreman guard: {what} uses the shared resource «{resource}»; run it inside `foreman lock {resource} run "what" command…` in the same call.
guard_deny: Blocked by the foreman guard: «{pattern}» is on the list of things never done without {owner} ({project}). Ask {owner} first (foreman backlog decision add, or the inbox).
guard_where_code: It matched in inline code (`{part}`), which is read as a command.
guard_where_sed: It matched in a sed or awk script (`{part}`), which is read as a command.
guard_where_loop: It matched in a loop or a test (`{part}`), which is read as a command.
guard_where_script: It matched in the script an interpreter reads (`{part}`).
guard_where_piped: It matched in text a shell runs (`{part}`).
guard_where_variable: It matched in a value given to a variable that runs (`{part}`).
guard_where_written: It matched in text written to a file that the same command line then runs (`{part}`).
guard_where_whole: The command could not be parsed (an unclosed quote, $'…', $((…))), so all its text was compared (`{part}`).
guard_where_tool: It matched in the place `{part}` the tool names, judged as a command that reads it (`cat PLACE`).
guard_where_resolved: It matched in the push as git would do it from `{dir}`: `{part}`.
guard_where_unknown: The folder of this push could not be known (a `cd` to a variable, `cd -`, a folder that does not exist), so it was checked against every repo of the project; it matched as git would do it from `{dir}`: `{part}`.
guard_how_resolved: The guard looks at where a push goes, not at how it is written. To push your own branch, name it (`git push origin BRANCH`); if the folder could not be known, write it literally (`cd /path/to/repo && git push …` or `git -C /path/to/repo push …`).
guard_how_tool: A tool's path or URL gets the verdict a command reading it would get; what a tool writes or sends as text (content, prompt, message) is not compared.
guard_how_text: If it is only text, write it with the Write or Edit tool, or with `cat > FILE <<'EOF'`.
guard_how_code: If it only edits text, use the Edit tool, or write the script to a file with the Write tool and run that file in a separate call.
guard_orchestrator_agent: Blocked by the foreman guard: «{pattern}» is run only by the orchestrator of {project}, with {owner}'s approval; never by an agent or a subagent. If your task needs it, say so in your report.
guard_orchestrator_session: Blocked by the foreman guard: «{pattern}» is run only by the orchestrator of {project} ({orchestrator}), and this session is not the marked one. If you relieve it, mark yourself first: `foreman session ID --name NAME`.
guard_orchestrator_process: Blocked by the foreman guard: «{pattern}» is run only by the orchestrator of {project} ({orchestrator}) from the Claude Code process that marked it, and this call runs in another one (a copy of the session), the mark records no process, or `ps` could not tell. If this is the orchestrator after a restart, mark yourself again: `foreman session ID --name NAME` (`foreman session` shows the process).
guard_orchestrator_grant: Blocked by the foreman guard: «{pattern}» is in the group «{group}», which also needs {owner}'s own yes, given to the orchestrator of {project} ({orchestrator}) for a while; there is none now. foreman's hooks module asks {owner} when the orchestrator runs it (with the module off, the group stays closed). After a no, do not try again until {owner} says so in the chat.
guard_hook_mod: Blocked by the foreman guard: `foreman hook mod` is run only by foreman's hooks module, never from a Bash call (not even by the orchestrator).
guard_panel_grant: Blocked by the foreman guard: the owner approves a pending request of a group in foreman's panel, by hand; no Bash call may reach that page's approval (not even the orchestrator's).
guard_permissions_apply: Blocked by the foreman guard: `foreman permissions apply` changes the permissions of {project}; only its orchestrator ({orchestrator}) runs it, from the marked session's main thread and process, after {owner}'s yes; never an agent or a subagent, nor another session. If your task needs a change of permissions, propose it in your report (a candidate tested with `foreman permissions --candidate`).
guard_main_checkout: Blocked by the foreman guard: `git {sub}` changes the files of {dir}, the main checkout that holds the live configuration of {project}; only its orchestrator does that there, never an agent or a subagent. Do it in your worktree (`git -C <your worktree> …` or `cd <your worktree> && git …`); to save or undo single files, limit it to them (`git stash push -- PATH`, `git checkout -- PATH`).
guard_integrate_agent: Blocked by the foreman guard: `foreman integrate` merges a branch into main and closes its backlog issue; only the orchestrator of {project} ({orchestrator}) runs it, never an agent or a subagent. Deliver with `foreman progress --done`; `foreman integrate … --check` and `--help` you may run.
guard_file: Blocked by the foreman guard: `{path}` is {what}, which no Write or Edit call changes.
guard_file_bash: Blocked by the foreman guard: this command writes `{path}`, which is {what}; no tool call or command changes that file (`{part}`).
guard_file_agent: Blocked by the foreman guard: `{path}` is {what}, which an agent does not change.
guard_file_bash_agent: Blocked by the foreman guard: this command writes `{path}`, which is {what}; an agent does not change it, with a tool call or a command (`{part}`).
guard_file_what_registry: foreman's list of the projects of this machine (the registry)
guard_file_what_git: part of the git hooks or configuration of a repo of {project}
guard_file_what_git_machine: part of this machine's git configuration (every repo reads it)
guard_file_how_perms: Only the orchestrator of {project} changes it, with `foreman permissions apply`, which tests the change first. If your task needs a change, write a candidate copy in your own folder, test it with `foreman permissions --candidate FILE`, and say so in your report.
guard_file_how_perms_orchestrator: Change it with `foreman permissions --candidate FILE` and then `foreman permissions apply FILE`, on a copy in your scratch folder: they test it, keep a copy of the live one, and ask {owner} when the change allows something new. Never by hand.
guard_file_how_state: Only foreman writes it (and the orchestrator its own board); a working script or a scratch file goes in your own scratch folder.
guard_file_how_owner: Only {owner} changes it, by hand: say what to change and where (in your report, or to {owner} in the chat).
guard_file_how_owner_ask: Only {owner} changes it: by hand, or with {owner}'s yes to the question foreman asks in this chat, for that one change. If no question came up, say what to change and where to {owner} in the chat.
guard_file_how_git: What an agent leaves there would run with the power of whoever runs git next in that repo (the orchestrator when it integrates, or {owner}), in no diff anyone reviews. For one command, use `git -c KEY=VALUE …`; if your task needs a hook or a setting of the repo, say so in your report (the orchestrator or {owner} sets it).
grant_question: {orchestrator}, the orchestrator of {project}, wants to run a command of the group «{group}»: `{command}`. Do you let it run the commands of «{group}» for {minutes} minutes?
grant_question_tool: {orchestrator}, the orchestrator of {project}, wants to use {tool} on `{command}`, which the group «{group}» covers. Do you let it run the commands of «{group}» and reach what they name for {minutes} minutes?
grant_denied_no: Blocked: {owner} said no to the group «{group}». Do not try again until {owner} says so in the chat; for {minutes} minutes foreman will not ask again.
grant_denied_dismissed: Blocked: {owner} closed the question about the group «{group}» without saying yes. Do not try again until {owner} says so in the chat.
grant_denied_timeout: Blocked: {owner} did not answer the question about the group «{group}» in time. The request waits for {owner} in foreman's panel; tell {owner} in the chat and do not try again until {owner} says so.
grant_denied_unavailable: Blocked: nobody could be asked about the group «{group}» in this session (no one at the prompt). Tell {owner} in the chat.
grant_denied_cooldown: Blocked: {owner} said no to the group «{group}» a moment ago; foreman will not ask again before {until}. Do not try again until {owner} says so in the chat.
grant_denied_waiting: Blocked: a question about the group «{group}» is already waiting for {owner}'s answer. Do not try again until {owner} says so in the chat.
grant_refused_session: Blocked: the yes for the group «{group}» came to a session that is no longer the marked orchestrator, so nothing was granted.
grant_refused_process: Blocked: the yes for the group «{group}» came to a Claude Code process that is not the one that marked the orchestrator, so nothing was granted.
grant_late: {owner}'s answer ({answer}) about the group «{group}» came after the question had expired: it is written down, nothing was granted.
grant_late_granted: {owner}'s answer ({answer}) about the group «{group}» came after the question had expired: it is written down and changes nothing; the group is already allowed until {until} ({via}).
grant_note_panel: grant «{group}»: {owner} approved from the panel the request of {asked} for {orchestrator}, until {until}: `{command}`
grant_panel_inbox: Approved from the panel: the group «{group}» is allowed until {until}. You may run again: `{command}`
grant_file_question: Do you let this session of {project} write `{path}`, {what}? It is for this one change only.
grant_file_question_bash: Do you let this session of {project} run `{command}`? It writes `{path}`, {what}. It is for this one command only.
grant_file_waiting: Blocked: a question about {what} is already waiting for {owner}'s answer. Do not try again until {owner} says so in the chat.
grant_file_long: Blocked: this command writes `{path}`, {what}, and is longer than {chars} characters, so foreman does not ask {owner} about it. Write that file in a command of its own, short enough to read whole, or with the Write or Edit tool.
grant_file_late: {owner}'s answer ({answer}) about writing `{path}` came after the question had expired: it is written down, nothing was allowed.
grant_file_log: `{path}` may be written once, this call
grant_file_denied_no: Blocked: {owner} said no to writing `{path}` ({what}). Do not try again until {owner} says so in the chat.
grant_file_denied_dismissed: Blocked: {owner} closed the question about writing `{path}` ({what}) without saying yes. Do not try again until {owner} says so in the chat.
grant_file_denied_timeout: Blocked: {owner} did not answer in time the question about writing `{path}` ({what}). Tell {owner} in the chat and do not try again until {owner} says so.
grant_file_denied_unavailable: Blocked: nobody could be asked in this session about writing `{path}` ({what}); nobody is in front of it. Tell {owner} what to change and where.

start.title: Start of an orchestrator session: {project} ({time})
start.you_unknown: not found ({how}): take the id from the newest `.jsonl` of this folder under the Claude Code projects folder
start.how_beat: as the live session of this folder (its heartbeat from foreman's hooks module)
start.how_beat_many: as the newest of the {n} live sessions of this folder (heartbeats from foreman's hooks module): check it is this one
start.how_transcript: as the newest transcript of this folder: check it is this session
start.how_none: no session id in the environment, no live session or transcript of this folder
start.verdict_unknown: alive or not cannot be told (no heartbeat from foreman's hooks module in it); last loop pass {last}
start.verdict_no_loop: alive, but no loop pass since {last}: foreman's hooks module makes no passes in it
start.verdict_silent: no loop pass since {last} and no heartbeat from foreman's hooks module in it: it may be gone
start.paused: PAUSED since {since} (from the panel): no integrate, worktree or launch until {owner} resumes it.
start.step_loop: The loop needs nothing from you: once this session is marked, foreman's hooks module sends it the pass, a prompt starting with «{prompt}», every {every} min (the first within a minute).
start.step_no_loop: No [loop] prompt in foreman.toml: no loop pass.
start.step_tell_out: Tell {name} (SendMessage) that you are marked: its passes stop and it closes.
start.step_out_gone: {name} is not alive: nobody to tell. Its agents that were live show below as dead: relaunch or `foreman agents --stop ID`.
start.step_owner: Tell {owner} in plain words (read `foreman docs owner` first) that the orchestrator session changed and why, and whether anything is asked of them.
start.step_pass: Then the pass: `foreman --project {project} loop` (the orchestrator-pass skill); the board below is your memory, rewrite it as you go.
start.board_none: (no board yet: write it as the session goes, ~15 lines of what only the orchestrator knows)
start.backlog: Active backlog ({n} issues; `foreman backlog show ID` for one)
start.rules: Rules: {path} ({kb} KB, ≈{tokens} tokens): read it once; it wins over the procedure. Sections: {headings}
start.next_owner: `foreman docs owner`: before your first message to {owner}.
start.next_procedure: `foreman docs orchestrator`: only the section a notice or a case asks for («Every pass», «Renewal», the notices table).
start.next_notes: today's notes {path} ({lines} lines): look things up with grep, never whole.
start.next_tools: `foreman agents`, `foreman catchup --json`: detail when a line above is not enough.

claude_min: foreman needs Claude Code ≥ {min} but this session runs {found}: run `claude update` (then restart Claude Code); until then parts of foreman may not work. Tell the owner.
claude_min_owner: foreman needs Claude Code ≥ {min} but this session runs {found}: run `claude update`.
who_other: This product ({project}) is orchestrated by the session {name} (since {since}); you are not its orchestrator: do not touch its backlog or launch production agents (if the orchestrator briefed you, follow your brief). To coordinate, write to {name} with SendMessage; shared resources only through `foreman lock RESOURCE run "what" cmd…`.
who_other_unnamed: This product ({project}) is orchestrated by the session {session}… (since {since}; it has no name for SendMessage); you are not its orchestrator: do not touch its backlog or launch production agents (if the orchestrator briefed you, follow your brief). Shared resources only through `foreman lock RESOURCE run "what" cmd…`.
who_none: This product ({project}) has no orchestrator now (no session marked with `foreman session`): do not take over its backlog or launch production agents unless the owner asks you to. Shared resources only through `foreman lock RESOURCE run "what" cmd…`.
who_gone: This product ({project}) is marked as orchestrated by the session {name} (since {since}), but that session is not alive: it ended, or foreman's hooks module has sent no heartbeat from it for 2 minutes (last loop pass {last}). If this session comes to relieve it, mark yourself with `foreman --project {project} session {session} --name <your name>` (the loop pass then comes to this session); otherwise tell {owner} and do not take over its backlog or launch production agents. Shared resources only through `foreman lock RESOURCE run "what" cmd…`.
who_silent: This product ({project}) is marked as orchestrated by the session {name} (since {since}), but its loop has made no pass since {last} (more than {limit} min) and it sends no heartbeat from foreman's hooks module, so whether it runs cannot be told: it may be gone. If this session comes to relieve it, mark yourself with `foreman --project {project} session {session} --name <your name>` (the loop pass then comes to this session); otherwise tell {owner} and do not take over its backlog or launch production agents. Shared resources only through `foreman lock RESOURCE run "what" cmd…`.
config_warnings: foreman ({project}): its configuration has warnings; it loads and works, ignoring what this foreman does not know, but `foreman check` fails until they are fixed or foreman is updated: {warnings}.
config_broken: foreman: the configuration of this product ({project}) does not load, so foreman's hooks are off here until it is fixed: the guard lets every command through (no [deny], no resource locks enforced) and no loop pass comes. Error: {error}. See `foreman --project {project} check`; until then, follow the project's rules by hand.
pause_line: PAUSED from the panel (since {since}): do not launch production agents or integrate (foreman worktree and foreman integrate are blocked) until {owner} resumes it there; answer the inbox, keep notes and let live agents finish.
pause_guard: Blocked by the foreman guard: {project} is paused from the panel (since {since}); `foreman {what}` waits until {owner} resumes it there.
pause_agents: Blocked by foreman: {project} is paused from the panel (since {since}); no production agent ({type}) is launched until {owner} resumes it there. Other agent types (planning, exploration) may run.
loop_idle: Loop pass {time}: nothing to do (skipped without calling the model).
band_failed: foreman: the status could not be read ({why})
status_outside: foreman: this folder is not in an active foreman project.
version_behind: This session runs foreman {mine} ({root}); {installed} is installed ({installed_root}). Claude Code keeps a session on the version it started with: its hooks and the `foreman` on its PATH stay {mine} until {owner} types `/reload-plugins` in this session (only they can) or resumes it. Tell {owner} once. Until then, what changed is in {installed_root}/CHANGELOG.md ({mine} → {installed}): a config key, a lock or a check added since may behave here as in {mine}.
version_replaced: This session runs foreman {mine} ({root}), and that install was replaced by a newer one (Claude Code marked its folder `.orphaned_at`; the new version is not known yet). Claude Code keeps a session on the version it started with: its hooks and the `foreman` on its PATH stay {mine} until {owner} types `/reload-plugins` in this session (only they can) or resumes it. Tell {owner} once. Until then, what changed is in the CHANGELOG.md of the new install (a sibling folder of {root}): a config key, a lock or a check added since may behave here as in {mine}.
version_behind_owner: foreman {mine} in this session, {installed} installed: type /reload-plugins
version_replaced_owner: foreman {mine} in this session was replaced by a newer install: type /reload-plugins
renew_owner: foreman: renewing this session's memory in place ({tokens} of {window} used); the work goes on in a minute
renew_done_owner: foreman: memory renewed in this session, {before} → {after}; the work goes on, nothing to do on your side
renew_low_owner: foreman: the memory renewal freed too little ({before} → {after}); foreman renews it again by itself when it reaches {force}, nothing to do on your side
renew_failed_owner: foreman: renewing this session's memory did not work ({why}); foreman tries again in {minutes} min
renew_failed_again_owner: foreman: renewing this session's memory did not work again ({why}); foreman tries again in {minutes} min, and you can also type /compact in this session when it suits you (foreman gives it back its memory after it)
renew_pack_head: foreman renewed this session's memory in place at {time} (context {before} before): Claude Code compacted it, and this is foreman's pack. You are still {name}, the marked orchestrator of {project}: the mark, the loop pass and your agents are as they were. Do not run `foreman start` or `foreman session`, and there is nothing to tell the owner (they saw it on screen). A loop pass comes within a minute: act on it as usual. The whole conversation before is in {transcript}: grep it when a detail is missing. This pack, whole, is in {pack}.
renew_pack_head_compact: This session's conversation was compacted at {time} (Claude Code's automatic compaction or a /compact), and this is foreman's pack. You are still {name}, the marked orchestrator of {project}: the mark, the loop pass and your agents are as they were. Do not run `foreman start` or `foreman session`. A loop pass comes within a minute: act on it as usual. The whole conversation before is in {transcript}: grep it when a detail is missing. This pack, whole, is in {pack}.
renew_pack_cut: … The pack is cut here to fit; the rest (backlog, owner's decisions, agents, rules) is in {pack}: read it before you act.
launch_line_missing: foreman: a production agent ({type}, {agent}) was launched without a launch line, so foreman cannot tie it to its name, issue and branch. Give it one now with `foreman agents --name {agent} NAME --issue ID --sub Tn --branch BRANCH`, and next time start the brief with the line `foreman launch` prints.
plain_echo: Your last message to the owner named without explaining: {items}. If you write about any of them again, say what it is (docs/owner.md); no need to resend that message.
catchup_from_default: no earlier catch-up: the last 24 h
catchup_from_capped: the last catch-up is older than 7 days: the last 7 days
catchup_idle: {n} in progress with no live agent: {ids}
catchup_approval: waiting for your approval to integrate: {why}
catchup_incomplete: let go with its delivery incomplete, missing: {missing}
catchup_ci_branch: the CI failed on a branch not integrated afterwards: {cmd}
catchup_loop_gap: no loop pass from {start} to {end} ({minutes} min; the limit is {limit} min)
perm_no_table: No guard table ([check] guard_table): no row checks any rule
perm_dropped: Inherited rules this product removes with [deny] drop ({n}): {rules}
perm_table_error: The guard table does not read: {error}
perm_orchestrator: Only the orchestrator, after {owner}'s yes (each yes lasts {minutes} min)
perm_apply_rule: foreman (its own rule): changing the permissions with `foreman permissions apply`; when it allows something new (--opens), after {owner}'s yes to the yes/no question
perm_main_checkout_rule: foreman (its own rule): an agent's git that rewrites a main checkout holding a live home (merge, pull, checkout of a branch, reset --hard, stash, restore or rm of a live file…): only the orchestrator, in any product
perm_integrate_rule: foreman (its own rule): `foreman integrate` (but --check and --help): only the orchestrator, never an agent
perm_turn: Waits its turn (inside `foreman lock RESOURCE run`)
perm_no_row: no row of the guard table checks it
perm_warn_no_row: Warning: {n} rules with no row in the guard table
perm_lifeline: What the orchestrator must keep ({n} commands, without any group)
perm_table_fails: {n} rows of the table fail with the candidate
perm_v_split: {agent} for an agent, {orchestrator} for the orchestrator
perm_base: Base for a candidate: {sha} (write `# foreman permissions base: {sha}` in the copy, or give `apply --base {sha}`)
perm_apply_no_base: the candidate does not say which foreman.toml it was copied from: nothing written. Write the line `# foreman permissions base: HASH` in it, or give --base HASH, with the hash `foreman permissions` showed when you copied it (if you no longer know it, copy foreman.toml again and redo the change).
perm_apply_changed: foreman.toml changed after the candidate was copied (base {base}, now {sha}): nothing written. Copy it again and redo the change.
perm_apply_opens: This change allows something that was not allowed before: nothing written. If {owner} said yes to it, run it again with --opens: foreman asks {owner} yes/no first.
perm_opens: What it allows that was not allowed before
perm_machine_heading: Machine candidate {candidate} against the registry {registry}: {n} products
perm_machine_outside: The candidate differs from the registry outside [machine]: only its [machine] is tested
perm_machine_groups: {n} rows would need the yes of several groups (one each), not as before
perm_machine_ok: No product loses a row of its table or a lifeline command
perm_machine_fails: A product loses a row of its table or a lifeline command, gets a warning or does not load (above)
perm_opens_minutes: each yes of a group lasts {after} min instead of {before}
perm_opens_command: {where}, a command foreman runs on its own with the orchestrator's power (the guard does not see it): {before} → {after}
perm_opens_brake: {where}, a brake of the integration comes off: {before} → {after}
perm_apply_fails: Nothing written: a row of the table fails or the orchestrator would lose a command (above).
perm_apply_no_table: --table {table} has nowhere to go: the candidate has no [check] guard_table. Nothing written.
perm_apply_same: The candidate and its table are the live ones: nothing written.
perm_apply_reload: foreman.toml did not load after the change ({error}): the previous one is back.
perm_applied: Applied: {files}. Copy of the previous ones: {backup}. To undo it: `{undo}`
perm_note_rows: {n} rows of the guard table change verdict
perm_note_opens: allows something new, with {owner}'s yes to the question (--opens)
perm_note_other: no rule or verdict changes (other keys, or the table)
perm_refused_total: Refused in the last {days} days: {n} (`foreman permissions --refused`)
perm_reserved: Reserved files (no session writes them with its tools, the orchestrator's neither, but as each line says)
perm_reserved_who_config: Changes only with `foreman permissions apply` (the orchestrator, after {owner}'s yes)
perm_reserved_who_table: Changes only with `foreman permissions apply`, with the configuration
perm_reserved_who_state: Written by foreman's own commands; the orchestrator writes its board ({board})
perm_reserved_who_registry: {owner} by hand, or a chat with {owner}'s yes, for that one change (never an agent); and foreman's own commands
perm_reserved_who_claude: {owner} by hand, or a chat with {owner}'s yes, for that one change (never an agent); Claude Code writes its own
perm_reserved_who_git: The orchestrator and {owner}'s sessions write them; an agent never (what it left there would run with their power). Reading them is free
perm_reserved_others: The same for the configuration, guard table, state and the git hooks and configuration of the repos of the {n} other registered products
integ_perm_head: permissions: {branch} changes live files of {product} ({files}), tested as `foreman permissions apply` would test it, on what {main} will hold
integ_perm_warning: Warning, this foreman does not know it (read without it): {warning}
integ_perm_repo_keys: Warning: the next integration refuses these [repos.*] keys until a foreman that knows them is installed: {keys}
integ_perm_also: Also changes (shown, the owner is not asked): {keys}
integ_perm_ok: the permissions only get stricter, or nothing that is allowed changes: the integration goes on
integ_perm_check_stop: --check: the integration would stop here, before the CI (exit {rc})
integ_perm_check_opens: --check: it allows something new: it would need --opens{given} ({owner}'s yes/no) before the CI
integ_perm_opens_given: it allows something new, with {owner}'s yes (--opens): the integration goes on
integ_perm_opens_unused: --opens: nothing the branch changes allows anything new; not needed
integ_perm_opens_stop: {branch} changes the permissions so that they allow something that was not allowed before (above): nothing merged, no CI. If {owner} says yes, run it again with --opens: foreman asks {owner} yes/no first
integ_perm_fails_stop: {branch} would make a row of the guard table fail or the orchestrator lose a command (above): nothing merged, no CI
integ_perm_broken_stop: {branch} would leave the product without a guard ({error}): nothing merged, no CI
integ_perm_progress: {repo}:{branch} waits for {owner}'s yes: it changes the permissions so that they allow something new
integ_perm_error: could not test the change of permissions ({error}): nothing merged
integ_perm_summary: permissions of {product}: {rules} rules and {rows} row verdicts change, {added} rows added, {removed} removed

init.check_none: (To fill in: the command that tells the code works.)
init.sample_title: A sample issue: move it, edit it or cancel it
init.sample_detail: foreman init made this issue so the backlog is not empty. Move it to backlog or ready, edit it, or cancel it; then ask the orchestrator for your first real issue in your own words.
init.sample_criterion: the owner has seen this issue on the board and moved, edited or canceled it
